lines.japanese: 突如──俺の意識は、群集とノイズの渾然と絡みあった只中に投げだされた。
lines.english: Without warning, my consciousness was hurled into a maelstrom of bodies and noise.

lines.japanese: 一瞬遅れて、自分が≪コックピット≫へ放りこまれたことと、冷たいコンクリートタイルの上にがっくり膝が落ちていることに気付いた。
lines.english: An instant later, I realized I had been thrown into the *Cockpit* and had collapsed to my knees on the cold concrete tiles.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どしたの平気？」
lines.english: “H-hey, what happened? Are you okay?”

lines.japanese: 知らない女が、片膝をついている俺に手を差しだした。俺はぶるんと頭を振って自力で立ちあがった。打ちつけた膝の皿と、首の後ろ──延髄のあたりが締めつけられるように鈍く痛んでいた。
lines.english: A woman I didn’t know held out a hand to me as I knelt there. I shook my head hard and stood on my own. The kneecap I’d struck and the back of my neck—right at the base of the skull—throbbed with a dull, constricting pain.

lines.japanese: くそっ、あの野郎≪スクランブル≫はやめろつってんのに……さては、またなんか都合悪くなって逃げだしたな、チキンが……。
lines.english: Damn it. I told that bastard not to *Scramble* me... Bet he ran into trouble again and fled. Fucking chicken...

lines.japanese: 「なに、立ちくらみ？」
lines.english: “What, did you get lightheaded?”

lines.japanese: 首の裏を手刀で叩いていると、女が俺の腕に手を添えようとした。馴れ馴れしい。俺は利き腕でそれを弾いた。
lines.english: As I thumped the back of my neck with the edge of my hand, the woman reached for my arm. Too damn familiar. I knocked her hand aside with my dominant arm.

lines.japanese: 「なんでもねえよ。ほっとけ」
lines.english: “It's nothing. Leave me alone.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん」
lines.english: “Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 今度は後ろから違う女が、チキン野郎の名を呼んで回りこんできた。温度の読めない目をしている。怒っているようにも悲しんでいるようにも見えた──どっちにしろ俺の苦手な目だ。
lines.english: This time a different woman called the chicken bastard’s name from behind me and came around to face me. I couldn’t read the feeling in her eyes. She might have been angry or sad—either way, they were the kind of eyes I couldn’t handle.

lines.japanese: 「話はだいたい飲みこめました」
lines.english: “I think I've got the gist.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺は全然」
lines.english: “Well, I sure don't.”

lines.japanese: 俺はふたりの女を遠ざける勢いで腕を横に振った。
lines.english: I swept an arm sideways with enough force to drive both women back.

lines.japanese: 「いいから。いいからとりあえず、いまはガタガタ騒ぐな。な。話あんなら今度聞くから──」
lines.english: “Enough. Just—enough. For now, quit making a fuss, all right? If you've got something to say, I'll hear you out next time—”

lines.japanese: ──俺じゃなくて、鷲介が。
lines.english: —or rather, Shusuke would.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 目を丸くしている女たちを無視して、俺は肩にかかっていたスポーツバッグを担ぎなおした。ともかくこんな、帰りの電車が待っている場所にいても意味がない。さっさと現場にでも向かおう。
lines.english: Ignoring the wide-eyed women, I hitched the sports bag back onto my shoulder. There was no point hanging around a place where everyone else had a train home waiting for them. I might as well head straight to the job site.

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょ、千歳君！？　どこ行くの、終電出ちゃうよ！」
lines.english: “W-wait, Chitose! Where are you going? The last train's about to leave!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 終電？
lines.english: The last train?

lines.japanese: 駅の出口へ向かおうとすると、女が不可解なことを言った。俺は時計を探した。コンコースの真ん中に吊り時計があった。時刻は２４時をちょっと過ぎていた。
lines.english: When I started toward the station exit, the woman said something I couldn't make sense of. I looked for a clock. One hung in the middle of the concourse. It was a little after midnight.

lines.japanese: に、２４時過ぎてるだァ？
lines.english: P-past midnight?
“What!?”

lines.japanese: なんでだよ。２２時までには交替する≪取り決め≫なのに、ヤロウ、また破りやがったな。ふざけやがって。土曜の夜はとくにこういうことが多い。
lines.english: Why the hell? Under the *Agreement*, we were supposed to switch by ten. That bastard had broken it again. What a load of shit. This happened especially often on Saturday nights.

lines.japanese: 「んだよ、ふざけんなよ……また俺が、ヒゲとかプリンに嫌味言われんじゃねーかチクショー……」
lines.english: “What the hell? Give me a break... Now Beard and Pudding Head are gonna give me shit again, goddammit...”

lines.japanese: 俺は見栄っ張りのチキン野郎に、思わず苦情を漏らした。どうせ≪コックピット≫から何を言ったところで、やつが引きこもった≪待機室≫に届きはしないんだけど。
lines.english: I couldn’t help complaining to that vain chicken bastard. Not that anything I said from the *Cockpit* could reach the *Waiting Room* he’d holed up inside.

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょっと何、君の彼氏どうしちゃったの？」
lines.english: “What...? Hey, what's gotten into your boyfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「か、彼氏じゃありませんっ！」
lines.english: “H-he is not my boyfriend!”

lines.japanese: 女たちはまだピーピー騒いでいた。もちろん俺は、気にも留めずに離れていった。
lines.english: The women were still squawking behind me. Naturally, I walked off without giving them another thought.

lines.japanese: 鷲介のクソは、ちょっと不審に思われたかもしれない。本当はもっと上手くやり過ごさなきゃいけない≪取り決め≫なんだけど、知るか、時間を守らずおまけに≪スクランブル≫までさせたのはやつの方だ。
lines.english: I’d probably made Shusuke look a little suspicious. The *Agreement* said we were supposed to play these things off more smoothly, but screw that. He was the one who ignored the schedule and forced a *Scramble* on me to boot.

lines.japanese: ホームへ向かう早足の人波に逆らって、俺は駅東口から外に出た。
lines.english: Fighting the fast-moving tide headed for the platforms, I went out through the station's east exit.

lines.japanese: 駅構内を出てしまえば雑踏の流れは淀む。前にも言ったよな。週末の柳木原は眠らない街なんだ。
lines.english: Once you left the station, the current of the crowd pooled and slowed. I told you before, didn’t I? Yanagihara was a city that never slept on weekends.

lines.japanese: 俺はスチールパイプの簡易ベンチに狭い空隙を見つけて近付いていった。隙間の横にいた三人組の女が迷惑そうに詰めて穴を広げた。俺は遠慮なく座った。女たちはすぐに会話を再開した。
lines.english: I spotted a narrow opening on one of the makeshift steel-pipe benches and headed for it. The three women beside the gap grudgingly squeezed together to make room. I sat without ceremony. They immediately resumed their conversation.

lines.japanese: 夜が更けてもアルバトロスの街頭ビジョンはお構いなしに騒音を撒きちらしている。でもみんなそんなことには構いもせず、好き勝手に土曜の夜を愉しんでいた。
lines.english: Even deep into the night, the Albatross outdoor screen went right on blasting noise everywhere. Nobody paid it any mind. They were all enjoying Saturday night however they damn well pleased.

lines.japanese: 銀細工を広げるマルチネスの露店も、素人のおねーさんに付きまとうプラチナの姿もないけど、やつらだってきっと今ごろはどこかで誰かと、飲んだり騒いだり乳繰りあったりしてるんだろう。
lines.english: Martinez wasn’t there with his silverwork spread out for sale, nor was Platinum pestering some woman who wasn’t in the trade. But they were probably off somewhere themselves by now, drinking, raising hell, or pawing at somebody.

lines.japanese: くそったれ。おうとも、俺はひとりでお仕事に精を出してやるさ。
lines.english: Goddammit. Fine. I'd go work my ass off all alone.

lines.japanese: 現場への道すがらピンフ通りを回っていってもいいけど、いつも１１時ぐらいで店を畳むあの走るクレープ屋はもうそこにいないはずだ。だからなんだって話。
lines.english: I could swing by Pinfu Street on the way to the site, but that mobile crêpe stand always packed up around eleven. It wouldn’t be there anymore. So what?

lines.japanese: 俺はなんとなく──なんとなくベロの先でほっぺの裏をつんつんしたくなってきたのでそうした。
lines.english: For some reason—no reason—I felt like prodding the inside of my cheek with the tip of my tongue, so I did.

lines.japanese: 三人組の女の前に三人組の男がやってきた。待ち合わせだったみたいだ。ひとしきり騒ぎたてたあと、六人は連れだって歩きだした。飲みでもカラオケでも乱交パーティでも好きにすればいい。
lines.english: Three men came over to the three women. Apparently they’d arranged to meet. After a round of excited squealing, all six walked off together. They could go drinking, sing karaoke, throw an orgy—whatever the hell they liked.

lines.japanese: しばらく俺は、駅舎の下で演ってるストリートバンドのサウンドに耳を傾けていた。だけどあんまり趣味に合わなかったから、聴くのをやめて交差点に向かった。
lines.english: For a while I listened to the street band playing beneath the station. They weren't much to my taste, so I quit listening and headed for the intersection.

lines.japanese: 皮肉や説教をいただきに職場へ向かうことを考えると、どうにも足が重かった。
lines.english: My feet felt unbearably heavy when I thought about heading to work to collect my ration of sarcasm and lectures.

lines.japanese: 横断歩道の手前で信号を待っていると、駄洒落ブタのものと同じ型のワンボックスがぬるい温風のように横切っていった（ドライバーと車体カラーは別モノだったけど）。
lines.english: While I waited at the crosswalk, a boxy van of the same model as Pun-Pig's drifted past like a breath of lukewarm air. Different driver and paint job, though.

lines.japanese: それで思いだす。ニワトリ軍団御一行は、ゆうべ高速道路の下を訪ねてこなかった。いや、来なくていいんだけど。今日は来るんだろうか。いや、来なくていいんだけど。
lines.english: That reminded me. The whole Chicken Army hadn't come calling beneath the expressway last night. Not that I wanted them to. Would they come tonight? Not that I wanted them to.

lines.japanese: 信号が青になった。俺は肩をほぐしながら歩きだした。
lines.english: The light turned green. I started walking, loosening my shoulders as I went.

lines.japanese: そのときだ。
lines.english: That was when it happened.

lines.japanese: 停止車線の前でタクシーやトラックが息をひそめ、歩行者のはしゃぎ声が偶然途切れたその一瞬。かすかに、甲高い太鼓の音が耳に触れた。
lines.english: For one instant, the taxis and trucks before the stop line held their breath, and the reveling pedestrians happened to fall silent. A faint, high-pitched drumbeat brushed my ear.

lines.japanese: 俺は梯子状の白ペンキの上で知らぬうちに速度を落とし、立ちどまり、ついにはきびすを返していた。
lines.english: Without realizing it, I slowed on the ladder of white paint, stopped, and finally turned on my heel.

lines.japanese: 四日ぶりのジェンベ。気まぐれな情熱。夜になると鳴きだすカラス。
lines.english: The djembe, after four days. A capricious passion. A crow that started calling after dark.

lines.japanese: 俺は遠い響きをたどって音の川上へさかのぼる。アフリカ太鼓の勇壮な響きに、重かった俺の歩みも少しばかり速くなった。
lines.english: I followed the distant beat upstream toward its source. The heroic pulse of the African drum put a little speed back into my leaden steps.

lines.japanese: 浅黒い肌の笑わない芸術家が柳木原に帰ってきたのか。
lines.english: Had the dark-skinned, unsmiling artist returned to Yanagihara?

lines.japanese: ステージネームはたしか、ハリュー・クロード。
lines.english: His stage name was Haryu Claude, if I remembered right.
